solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Key in "regret" and save

indicators.note: the word for the key is placed inside the word for regret

parts.note: to rue is to regret
Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone presses a key labelled 'regret' and saves their work, like an undo button.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'regret' look like a key's label, but it is only a word to replace with its synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to save them from danger, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Used to be left immediately

definitions.meaning: people who used to be politically on the left are, at present, on the right
at this very moment, without delay

explanation.surface: Something that was once abandoned is suddenly mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a political joke: those who once were left-wing are now on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at this instant, a synonym for without delay.

clue.text: To make an effort overcoming depression, it stops a lot

indicators.note: the effort word sits over and around the word for depression, enclosing it

parts.note: to strain is to make an effort
a low is an area of low pressure or a depression

explanation.surface: Someone struggling with depression keeps having to stop and rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it stops a lot' describes a stopping service that calls at every station.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow train is a rail service that calls at many stations, so it halts frequently.

clue.text: Instruction to keep reading university's first indication of responsibility

indicators.note: the first letter of the word university is taken

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, is printed at the foot of a page

explanation.surface: A note on a university form asks readers to continue, hinting at who is responsible.
explanation.walkthrough: The university letter comes first in the answer although the clue mentions it second.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a decision is 'up to you' marks you as the one accountable, so the phrase signals duty.

clue.text: Line in test script makes for difficulties

indicators.note: the letter for line is placed within the combined test and script words

parts.note: to probe is to test or examine
MS is short for manuscript, a script

explanation.surface: A single line in an exam script causes trouble for the candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside PROBEMS, between PROB and EMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Problems are troubles or difficulties, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Relax muscle in deference

indicators.note: the muscle word is placed inside the word for relax

parts.note: to rest is to relax
pec is short for pectoral muscle

explanation.surface: A gym instruction: ease the muscle out of courtesy.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing deference means showing esteem or regard, the same as respect.

clue.text: Fries you bring finally need a couple of bits of artificial sweetener

parts.note: fries as a verb means cooks until browned, so browns

indicators.note: the last letters of the words you and bring are taken
the first two letters of the word artificial are taken

explanation.surface: A diner asks for chips and a couple of sachets of artificial sweetener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fries' looks like chips but is a verb: browns. 'need' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This unrefined cane product is used to sweeten food and drink.

clue.text: Woman priest getting the support of South Africa

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece comes below, so after the priest

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel
ZA is the international code for South Africa

explanation.surface: A female priest finds backing from South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza is a female first name, so an example of a woman.

clue.text: Mounts up before quarter-horse's dash

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the mountain word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Alps are mountains, mounts
S, for south, is one quarter of the compass
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A rider climbs onto a quarter horse before galloping off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter-horse' looks like the American breed but splits into a compass point and slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash of a liquid is a small amount, as is a splash, e.g. of milk in tea.

clue.text: Politician invades foreign country to establish imperium

indicators.note: the politician goes into the country's name, entering it

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician invades another nation to set up imperial rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperium is supreme power or dominion, and an empire is a realm under such rule.

clue.text: Benefits include back issue of The Age of Prosperity

indicators.note: the benefits word takes the turned issue word inside it

parts.note: goods are benefits or advantages

indicators.note: back means the word for issue is read in reverse

parts.note: to emit is to issue or give out

explanation.surface: A back issue of a newspaper called The Age reports on welfare in boom years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back issue' looks like an old newspaper copy, and The Age is indeed an Australian paper, but 'back' simply reverses the verb for issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Good times means a period of plenty, an era of prosperity.

clue.text: College professor I elected to be largely ignored

indicators.note: most of the phrase is disregarded, leaving only letters inside it

explanation.surface: A college professor was elected but then mostly ignored by colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel is one of the colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: Cheers oddly thin film-maker

parts.note: ta is a British informal word for thanks, like cheers

indicators.note: the first and third letters of the word thin are taken

explanation.surface: A drinker thanks a strangely skinny director.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Tati was a French director known for Monsieur Hulot's Holiday.

clue.text: Curiosity could discover this in flames or destroyed

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: An inquisitive person finds something burning or wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: Curiosity is the NASA rover exploring Mars, not the human trait.
explanation.definitionFit: The rover was sent to look for signs that the red planet could support living things.

clue.text: One key state American devastated to relax

indicators.note: the combined letters are ruined and rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A key American state is wrecked, and people are told to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: IKEYSTATEA is the fodder for 'devastated'; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for unwinding or not overdoing things.

clue.text: Skeletal axolotl returns carrying salt

indicators.note: returns says the hidden letters are read backwards
the two words carry the answer's letters within them, across the word break

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bony salamander comes back carrying salt in its mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'carrying salt' as the definition, leaving the hidden word with no indicator; 'carrying' is that indicator and 'salt' alone defines. 'returns' reads the hidden letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxalate is a salt of oxalic acid, so the answer is an example of a salt.

clue.text: German out cycling caught in reverse trap

indicators.note: the cycled word is held inside the turned trap word
the word for trap is read backwards

parts.note: a net is a trap

indicators.note: the first letter of the word out moves to the end

explanation.surface: A German going out on a bike is caught in a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the first letter of 'out' to its end and 'reverse' turns the trap word round; the first then sits inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A Teuton is a member of an ancient Germanic people, so loosely a German.

clue.text: Where I heard the news of horrible rainy doom?

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are made into a dreadful jumble

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they learned of grim rainy weather from the broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of RAINYDOOM gives the answer; it is also the title of a song by The Selecter.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio set is a place one hears news bulletins, so the phrase locates the listening.

clue.text: It's a Nordic trait to squander energy agreement

parts.note: to blue money is old British slang for squandering it
E is the physics symbol for energy
yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: Wasting energy over consensus is said to be typical of Scandinavians.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale irises are a common feature among Scandinavians, so the colour is called a Nordic characteristic.

clue.text: Holy figure round Dundee?

parts.note: an angel is a heavenly being
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A saintly figure tours the Scottish city of Dundee.
explanation.walkthrough: Dundee looks like the city in Scotland but is a surname: Angelo Dundee trained Muhammad Ali.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark marks a definition by example: the boxing trainer's first name.

clue.text: Working lecturer too wise to be heard at university the sole person solving this?

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on

indicators.note: the words too wise are taken by their spoken form, two Ys

parts.note: the phrase spoken sounds like two Ys, a pair of letter Y
the OU is the Open University in Britain

explanation.surface: A busy lecturer too clever by half wonders if only one person will solve this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link. The OU is Britain's Open University.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase addresses a single person, the only one who can manage the clue.

clue.text: Confine contents of gallery brought back by Frenchwoman to London opening

indicators.note: the word for a gallery's contents is reversed

parts.note: a gallery contains art
Mme, Madame, is the French title for a married woman

indicators.note: the first letter of the word London is taken

explanation.surface: A French lady returns the gallery's exhibits to London for its opening.
explanation.definitionFit: To trammel is to hamper or restrict freedom, so to confine.

clue.text: Fill with wonder, but not as fashionable

indicators.note: the word as is removed from the longer word

parts.note: to astonish is to fill with wonder

explanation.surface: Something amazes, though not because it is stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonish is an old word for stylish or in the current mode.

clue.text: Happy at second very attractive result

parts.note: up means in good spirits
hot means very attractive

explanation.surface: Someone happy at once finding something attractive gets an outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot is the outcome or eventual consequence of something.

clue.text: Directly west possibly vacant

parts.note: west is an example of a compass point
blank means empty or vacant

explanation.surface: Heading straight west, perhaps to an empty place.
explanation.definitionFit: Point-blank as an adverb means straightforwardly and bluntly, as in refusing outright.

clue.text: Upside-down cereal misses small intestine

indicators.note: the letter for small is left out
in a down entry, upside-down means the cereal word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: muesli is a breakfast cereal

explanation.surface: A bowl of cereal tipped over misses the small intestine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upside-down' turns MUESLI into ILSEUM; 'misses' drops its S.
explanation.definitionFit: The ileum is the final section of the small intestine, so a part of the gut.

clue.text: Turkey rejecting Brussels — honest!

parts.note: TR is the international code for Turkey

indicators.note: the Brussels word is turned back on itself

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU, so stands for it

explanation.surface: Turkey is spurned by the European Union, and that's the truth!
explanation.definitionFit: As an exclamation, true means the speaker is being sincere, like saying honestly.

clue.text: Hired soldier as host to welcome queen

indicators.note: the host takes the queen inside, receiving her

parts.note: an MC, master of ceremonies, hosts an event
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a queen

explanation.surface: A mercenary acts as host to greet a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Merc is short for mercenary, a soldier paid to fight.

clue.text: Predator's heavy coat new in the middle of ice age

indicators.note: the coat of the word heavy is its outside letters
the letter for new goes inside the middle pair
the central letters of the phrase ice age are taken

explanation.surface: An animal hunter has a thick coat for the cold of an ice age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Predator's' means the predator is; N sits inside EA, the centre of ICEAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is an African carnivore that hunts as well as scavenges.

clue.text: Amazingly starry-eyed, having lost a hand in the very recent past

indicators.note: the letters are thrown into an astonishing new order

parts.note: R stands for right, as in right hand

explanation.surface: A dreamy romantic lost a hand in some recent mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost' removes R from STARRYEYED before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: The previous day is the very recent past, also used loosely for not long ago.

clue.text: Order to do exercise backwards found in barrel of weapon

indicators.note: the order and exercise pieces sit inside the barrel word

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel
OM is the Order of Merit

indicators.note: the exercise word is read in reverse

parts.note: gym is physical exercise, as in a gym class

explanation.surface: A drill instructor orders press-ups down the barrel of a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barrel' looks like part of the gun but is a cask, TUN. 'backwards' turns GYM into MYG.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thompson submachine gun is a firearm, a type of weapon.

clue.text: Repeats point about residential care facilities losing money

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
c, circa, means about

indicators.note: the letter for money is dropped

parts.note: care homes provide residential care

explanation.surface: A report repeats that care homes are running out of funds.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, echoes means repeats back what was said.
